**Triage: `priority:p2` · `pm:queue` · `domain:spec` · type `Task`.** First grading, `finding` comes off.

**Same class as #14369 (graded this shift), and the same answer on the unit of work: ⛔ this card is not "decide enforce-or-remove for two keys".** ADR-0049's route runs through the liveness ledger, and the `spec-property-retirement` playbook's entry condition is a ledger verdict. ⇒ **The deliverable is both keys landed in `packages/spec/liveness/api.json` with the evidence this card already measured** — and nothing else in that PR: no key enforced, removed, re-described or repointed.

⚠️ **Collision worth knowing before you start:** #14369 is queued to write ten *other* keys into that same ledger file. ⛔ Not a `Blocked-by:` — different keys, no ordering dependency — but the two PRs will conflict on `api.json` if they run concurrently. Whoever starts second rebases; whoever starts first says so on the other card.

## One narrowing the ledger entry should carry, because it is measurable now

The card asks "repoint `RealtimeEventType` at the emitted vocabulary, **or** make the runtime emit the declared one, whichever is the intended contract". Those are not symmetric:

- `data.record.created` / `.updated` / `.deleted` is declared in `packages/spec/src/api/events.zod.ts:139-141` **and** has a live emitter (`knowledge-service-plugin.ts:168`);
- `record.*` has **no runtime reader at all** — the card's own measurement finds only the enum's unit test and the alias pin.

⇒ The emitted vocabulary is the established one. If the verdict is **enforce**, it means **repointing the enum**; ⛔ it does not mean changing what the runtime publishes, which would break a live event contract to satisfy a member nothing has ever used. Write that into the ledger entry so the next reader does not re-open a settled direction.

**p2, with the zero-usage reading stated rather than ignored.** Realtime subscription authoring has **0** usages across `examples/**` and `packages/apps/**`, and I am not inflating that. It sits at p2 for the same reason #14369 does: this is a **published authoring surface where every member is wrong**, not merely unread. An author who writes the enum's own `record.created` gets a subscription that silently never fires — and the enum is what the API reference shows them. Latent, but customer-facing when it fires.

**`filters: z.unknown().optional()` is the easier half** — an authorable key with no shape and no consumer, which is the textbook ADR-0049 fourth state. It should reach the ledger with the same evidence and, if the verdict is remove, go through ADR-0087 like any other retirement.

**#4673 is the useful precedent and the card is right to name it**: `DataEventType`'s `data.field.changed` with no producer, same fourth state in the sibling enum, already closed. ⇒ Check how that one was disposed of before proposing a verdict here; a second answer to the same question in the same file family would be its own defect.

Size/model suggestion: S, `sonnet` — the measurement is done; the work is transcribing it into the ledger format and re-running it at a pinned ref.

Read the gate's header first; if `SubscriptionSchema` is not governed by `api.json`, a new ledger file enrolled the same way is the correct landing and the triage's file name is a drift, not a ruling — say so in the report. (b) The two rows are `SubscriptionSchema.type` (accept set `RealtimeEventType` — the declared spelling `record.*` vs the emitted `data.record.*`; note the direction narrowing verbatim from the triage) and `SubscriptionSchema.filters` (`z.unknown().optional()`, no shape, no reader). Both read as the ledger's dead/unenforced state on the evidence measured; re-take every reading at your worktree's base and quote it with the ref (symbol-anchored evidence, the ledger's own row format — read two existing rows and `liveness/README.md` before writing). If the ledger's schema also wants the other `SubscriptionSchema` keys classified when a schema is first enrolled (the RestServerConfig precedent classified every authorable property of the enrolled sub-objects), do that — it is the enrolment's own rule, not scope creep; say which keys and why. (c) `check:liveness` regenerates `liveness/state-counts.md`; run it and commit the follower. (d) Changeset: `liveness/**` is in the tarball's `files`, so a `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/spec` (PR #14638's precedent); no BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 marker.

**PM suggested route (optional).** Follow PR #14638's shape end to end (changeset text included); the `SubscriptionSchema.type` row's note carries the settled direction; the `filters` row's note names the textbook fourth state and the removal route as the likely verdict for the follow-up card — ⛔ no removal here.

**Surface, gates, report.** File surface = the claim comment 5536555785 (stop on breach). Before touching `liveness/**`, read the file list of the open branch `claude/issue-14442-package-record-serializable` and of the in-flight lane PRs (#14971 → `api/events.zod.ts`, #14414 → `automation/execution.zod.ts`) — report any overlap. Derive gates from your actual paths after the last commit (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands`, no path args — it reads the change set itself); at minimum `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:liveness`, `check:generated`, `check:published-files`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check-system-context-census`, the changeset gate self-tests. Report: `os-dev-report` first as a comment here, then as the return; machine-checkable fields only (status, pr, premise_still_valid, files_changed, gates pinned to the head sha, deviations, open_questions, out_of_scope_findings filed as cards after a dedup search).
